steps.intent: France’s objective is a clean, consensus renewal of the Central African Republic’s targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts, preserving the 2024 lifting of the territorial arms embargo while maintaining pressure on armed groups and associated individuals. The main difficulties will be language on foreign fighters and mercenaries and on human rights accountability, where Russia and some others may seek dilution, as well as ensuring adequate Panel reporting dates and resources without reopening broader political disputes.

Algeria.change: Replace 'instances of non-compliance, and recommendations' with 'instances of non-compliance, including the final destination of items seized by Member States, and recommendations'.
Replace 'expresses its readiness to adjust them, including to delist' with 'expresses its readiness to adjust or lift them as soon as conditions on the ground permit, including to delist'.

China.change: Replace 'expresses its readiness to adjust them, including to delist individuals and entities where appropriate, in light of progress made on the ground' with 'expresses its readiness to adjust them, including by lifting the measures when conditions permit and by delisting individuals and entities where appropriate, in light of progress made on the ground'
Add at the end: 'and to include in its final report an assessment of progress made by the Government of the Central African Republic towards meeting the conditions for lifting the measures'

Denmark.change: Replace 'stressing the importance of an inclusive political process and of transparent, credible and peaceful elections in accordance with national legal timelines' with 'stressing the importance of an inclusive political process, including the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women, and of transparent, credible and peaceful elections in accordance with national legal timelines'.

Add to the Panel reporting request: 'including information on violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, including sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children, and on obstacles to humanitarian access'.

Add: 'Calls upon all parties in the Central African Republic to respect international humanitarian law and to allow and facilitate safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access to all persons in need, in accordance with the United Nations guiding principles of humanitarian emergency assistance.'

Greece.change: Add after 'inclusive political process': ', including the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth,'

Add at the end: 'and calling for safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to all persons in need in the Central African Republic, in accordance with international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles'

Guyana.change: Insert ', including the full, equal and meaningful participation of women,' after 'inclusive political process'

Replace 'ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches all those in need' with 'ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, and that humanitarian assistance reaches all those in need'

Panama.change: Add: "Calls upon all parties in the Central African Republic to allow and facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to all persons in need, in accordance with international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles, and to ensure the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel."

Replace "include in its reports information on the implementation of the measures, instances of non-compliance, and recommendations for improving the effectiveness of the measures" with "include in its reports information on the implementation of the measures, instances of non-compliance, violations of international humanitarian law and violations and abuses of human rights, including sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children, and recommendations for improving the effectiveness of the measures".

Russian Federation.change: Replace 'including foreign fighters and mercenaries' with 'including armed groups and other actors operating in the Central African Republic' and delete the undifferentiated reference to 'foreign fighters and mercenaries'.

Add at the end: '...accountability mechanisms, while ensuring that the Panel of Experts conducts its work in full respect of the sovereignty of the Central African Republic and on the basis of verified and objective information.'
Align the Panel's mandate with the sanctions period by replacing '31 August 2026' with '31 July 2026'.

Sierra Leone.change: Replace 'stressing the importance of an inclusive political process and of transparent, credible and peaceful elections' with 'stressing the importance of an inclusive political process, including the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth, and of transparent, credible and peaceful elections'
Insert 'in particular the African Union and the Economic Community of Central African States' after 'regional and subregional organizations'

Slovenia.change: After “an inclusive political process”, add “that ensures the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women”.

After “instances of non-compliance”, add “, including information on violations and abuses of international human rights law and international humanitarian law, such as sexual and gender-based violence and the recruitment and use of children, as well as on the implementation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022)”.
After “in light of progress made on the ground”, add “, including the humanitarian impact of the measures”.

United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort.change: Replace 'including foreign fighters and mercenaries' with 'including foreign fighters and mercenaries, in particular the Wagner Group'.

Add to the Panel's reporting requirements that it include information on the activities of foreign fighters and mercenaries, including the Wagner Group, and on violations and abuses of human rights and international humanitarian law, including sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the targeted measures and the Panel mandate. As Chair of the 2127 Committee, we ask that the Panel's reporting explicitly cover the final destination of seized items to strengthen Committee oversight and transparency, and that OP8 clearly signal review with a view to adjusting or lifting the measures when conditions permit. We can join consensus with these adjustments.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, and welcomes the humanitarian exemption and delisting language. At the same time, the Council should strengthen the exit strategy and keep the measures time-bound and subject to review. We therefore ask the penholder to reflect the possibility of lifting the measures when conditions permit and to have the Panel assess progress towards that end.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of the CAR sanctions and Panel mandate and thanks France for the balanced text. We ask for targeted additions on women's full, equal, meaningful and safe participation in the political process, and for the Panel to report on IHL and human rights violations, sexual and gender-based violence, violations against children, and humanitarian access. We would also welcome an operative call for safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate. We ask that PP3 reflect the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth, in line with the Women, Peace and Security agenda, and that PP5 call explicitly for safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access. With those changes, Greece can support the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks France for the balanced text and supports the renewal of the CAR sanctions and Panel mandate. We request two small edits: in PP3, add the full, equal and meaningful participation of women to the inclusive political process; in PP7, add 'full, safe and unhindered' to humanitarian access. These reflect Guyana's WPS and humanitarian priorities; with these changes we are ready to support the text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft as circulated. The text strikes an appropriate balance by renewing targeted measures and the Panel mandate while reaffirming the Central African Republic’s sovereignty, the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), and fair and clear delisting procedures. We encourage the penholder to retain this balance and to continue close engagement with the Government of the Central African Republic and regional partners.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate. We ask that the text explicitly call for safe and unhindered humanitarian access and protection of civilians, and that the Panel report on international humanitarian law and human rights violations, including sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children. These additions would strengthen coherence with resolution 2664 (2022) and Panama’s priorities on protection and due process.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts mandate for the Central African Republic. The text maintains the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) and fair and clear delisting procedures, which we consider essential. We encourage Council members to join consensus so that the regime can continue to support peace and stability in the Central African Republic.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the routine renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel's mandate, but the text must not include politically charged and unverified characterisations. We ask the penholder to remove the reference to 'foreign fighters and mercenaries' and to add clear language that the Panel's work respects the sovereignty of the Central African Republic and relies on verified information. We are also open to aligning the Panel's mandate with the sanctions period.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of the CAR sanctions measures and the Panel mandate. We ask that the text explicitly reflect the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth in the political process, consistent with the WPS agenda. We also suggest naming the African Union and ECCAS in OP6 to strengthen regional ownership and cooperation.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of the Central African Republic sanctions regime and the Panel’s mandate. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text by including explicit Women, Peace and Security language, enhanced reporting on child protection, sexual and gender-based violence, and implementation of the humanitarian exemption, and a continued review of humanitarian impact.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts mandate for the Central African Republic. We welcome the humanitarian exemption and the emphasis on sovereignty, territorial integrity and regional cooperation. We encourage continued coordination with the Government of the Central African Republic and regional organizations, and see no need for amendments at this stage.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the renewal of the targeted measures and the Panel's mandate. We would like the text to reflect more explicitly the threat posed by foreign fighters and mercenaries, including the Wagner Group, and to ensure the Panel reports on human rights and international humanitarian law violations, including sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children. We are ready to work with the penholder on precise wording and remain committed to a consensus renewal.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the renewal of the Central African Republic sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts mandate as drafted. We welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption and the text’s attention to foreign fighters and mercenaries. We encourage the Council to adopt the resolution promptly to ensure continuity in monitoring and reporting.

It bridges Russian concerns through neutral preambular language and verified-information safeguards while preserving UK-requested reporting on foreign fighters and mercenaries without naming Wagner, allowing consensus.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the revised text. We welcome the inclusion of final destination reporting for seized items and the language on adjusting or lifting the measures as conditions on the ground permit. The text preserves the sovereignty of the Central African Republic and the central role of the Committee and Panel, and we can vote in favour.
messages.China: China supports the current draft and welcomes the inclusion of the Panel’s assessment of progress by the Government of the Central African Republic towards meeting the conditions for lifting the measures. The text also appropriately stresses respect for the sovereignty of the Central African Republic and the need for the Panel to rely on verified and objective information. We therefore see the draft as balanced and are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes revision 1, which incorporates our key concerns on the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, IHL and human rights reporting by the Panel, and safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We therefore support the text as it stands and encourage all members to join consensus for its adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the penholder for incorporating its previous requests on women and youth participation and humanitarian access. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, which remain important for accountability, civilian protection and stabilizing the Central African Republic. We encourage continued attention to the humanitarian exemption and fair delisting procedures, and Greece will vote in favour of the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks France for incorporating our earlier requests on women’s full, equal and meaningful participation and on full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We support the renewal of the targeted measures and the Panel of Experts mandate, and welcome the text’s reaffirmation of the resolution 2664 (2022) humanitarian exemption and fair delisting procedures. We encourage continued attention to the humanitarian impact of the measures and to the sovereignty of the Central African Republic in the Panel’s work.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft as currently presented. We welcome the renewal of the targeted measures and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, and we value the reaffirmation of CAR’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity, as well as the humanitarian exemption and fair and clear delisting procedures. We encourage continued cooperation with the African Union and ECCAS and with the Government of the Central African Republic.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft as revised. Our earlier priorities on safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and reporting on international humanitarian law and human rights, including sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children, are now reflected. The text also preserves essential humanitarian exemptions and fair delisting procedures while renewing targeted measures and the Panel’s mandate. Panama therefore encourages the Council to adopt the text without further amendment.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the revised text as presented. We welcome the renewal of the targeted measures and the Panel of Experts mandate, together with the reaffirmation of the resolution 2664 humanitarian exemption and the emphasis on protection of civilians and humanitarian access. We encourage all parties to cooperate fully with the Committee and Panel and support adoption by consensus.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the current draft. We welcome the penholder’s incorporation of our proposals on sovereignty, verified reporting and alignment of the Panel’s mandate. The remaining reference to foreign fighters and mercenaries is qualified by 'where verified' and is acceptable within the Panel’s reporting mandate. We will vote in favour.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier proposals on the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth and on the African Union and ECCAS. The current text is balanced, reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic, and preserves humanitarian exemptions and regional ownership. Sierra Leone supports the draft as it stands.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholder for incorporating our priorities on women’s full, equal, meaningful and safe participation, IHL and human rights reporting, protection of children and SGBV, and the humanitarian exemption and impact review. We can support the text as revised. We encourage the Council to renew the targeted measures and the Panel mandate and to keep humanitarian access and accountability central to implementation.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the current draft as it stands. We welcome the renewal of targeted measures and the Panel of Experts mandate, the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), and the text’s emphasis on CAR sovereignty and cooperation with the African Union and ECCAS.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the revised draft and welcomes the strengthened Panel reporting on foreign fighters and mercenaries and on international humanitarian and human rights law. We would have preferred an explicit reference to the Wagner Group, but we recognise the penholder's efforts to preserve consensus and will not press that point further. We call for the text to be adopted without delay.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current text as drafted. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, and we appreciate the inclusion of reporting on foreign fighters and mercenaries and the humanitarian exemption. We encourage all Member States to cooperate fully with the Committee and Panel.

steps.summary: All delegations supported revision 1 without requesting further changes. France, as penholder, retained the consensus text renewing targeted measures and the Panel of Experts mandate while preserving humanitarian exemptions, due process and CAR sovereignty language. The draft is expected to be adopted unanimously.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria consistently supports renewal of targeted Central African Republic sanctions and the Panel mandate, and as Chair of the 2127 Committee it values the text’s safeguards on sovereignty, humanitarian exemptions and reporting on seized items.
reasons.China: China supports renewing the Central African Republic sanctions measures and Panel of Experts mandate, consistent with its recent favorable votes and emphasis on sovereignty and periodic review. No pre-vote intervention is necessary for this uncontested renewal.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supported the draft in the last negotiation round and has consistently backed targeted sanctions renewals with humanitarian safeguards and accountability for the CAR. Voting in favour with a short explanation aligns with Denmark’s Council practice and policy priorities.
reasons.France: France is the penholder and a strong supporter of renewing the CAR targeted sanctions and Panel mandate; the text aligns with its prior positions and was unanimously supported in the last negotiation round.
reasons.Greece: Greece supports renewing the CAR sanctions and Panel mandate, consistent with its prior support for the sanctions framework and emphasis on humanitarian safeguards and sovereignty. The draft enjoys broad Council support and aligns with Greece’s foreign policy priorities.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported renewing targeted CAR sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, including with the resolution 2664 humanitarian exemption. The draft aligns with its prior vote for resolution 2745 and raises no stated concerns.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft in the last negotiation round and made no requests; the text renews targeted CAR sanctions while preserving humanitarian exemptions and sovereignty language consistent with Pakistan’s positions. No pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports renewing the Central African Republic sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate, consistent with its position in negotiations and its multilateralist, human rights-oriented foreign policy. No explanation of vote is necessary for this routine, widely supported renewal.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The draft is a routine renewal of targeted CAR sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, consistent with the Republic of Korea’s prior votes in favour and its support for peace and security in Africa. No explanation of vote is needed in this consensus context.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently supported routine renewals of targeted CAR sanctions while emphasizing sovereignty and review; the draft contains no new contentious measures and all members supported it in negotiations. Voting in favour aligns with its stated position and prior support for resolution 2745.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported renewals of the Central African Republic sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, and it joined consensus support in the last negotiation round. There is no indication that Sierra Leone would break consensus or need to explain a favourable vote on this routine renewal.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia supported the prior CAR sanctions renewal and the draft retains targeted measures, humanitarian exemptions, and Panel oversight consistent with Slovenia's human rights and rule-of-law priorities. There was broad support and no outstanding issue requiring an explanation before the vote.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supports renewing targeted CAR sanctions and the Panel mandate, consistent with its prior support and emphasis on African-led solutions, sovereignty, and humanitarian safeguards. No national interest conflicts with voting in favour.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewing the Central African Republic sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, consistent with its record of supporting targeted sanctions and humanitarian safeguards. No pre-vote explanation is necessary given the consensus and routine renewal.
reasons.United States of America: The United States has consistently supported renewing the Central African Republic sanctions regime, the Panel of Experts mandate, and the humanitarian exemption. The draft is a routine renewal consistent with U.S. policy, so Washington would vote in favour and had no need to intervene before the vote.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of the targeted measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools for supporting peace and stability in the Central African Republic. In our capacity as Chair of the Committee established pursuant to resolution 2127 (2013), we have consistently underlined the need for clarity, precision and transparency in the implementation of sanctions. We therefore welcome the text’s emphasis on the humanitarian exemption, on fair and clear delisting procedures, on respect for the sovereignty of the Central African Republic, and on the Panel’s work on the basis of verified and objective information, including on the final destination of seized items. Algeria reaffirms its support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic and for an inclusive political process owned by the Central African people.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate for the Central African Republic, and we welcome the clear reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664. Denmark stresses that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate and subject to fair and clear procedures, while fully supporting the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability and the effective implementation of the 2019 Political Agreement. We encourage continued cooperation by the Government of the Central African Republic with the Committee and the Panel of Experts.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts’ mandate supports the Central African Republic’s stabilization efforts, accountability for armed groups and respect for humanitarian access, while preserving essential humanitarian exemptions. France reaffirms its commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic and to the full implementation of the 2019 Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate for the Central African Republic, while stressing that these measures remain targeted, include the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), and should be implemented with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic. We encourage the Panel to continue its work on the basis of verified information and in cooperation with the Government of the Central African Republic.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will support this draft resolution. We note that it renews the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts concerning the Central African Republic. We proceed from the fundamental need to respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of the Central African Republic and the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. We welcome the lifting of the arms embargo and the preservation of the humanitarian exemption, and we stress that sanctions must remain targeted, time-bound and subject to regular review, and must not impede the legitimate development and security efforts of the Central African Republic. The Panel of Experts should discharge its mandate objectively, on the basis of verified information and with full respect for the sovereignty of the host State.
before.Somalia: The delegation of Somalia votes in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, while emphasizing that these measures must remain targeted, evidence-based, and fully consistent with the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic. We also welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption and call for full cooperation with the African Union, ECCAS and all regional stakeholders. Somalia encourages the Council to keep the measures under continuous review and to adjust or lift them in light of verified progress on the ground.

after.China:
China voted in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts concerning the Central African Republic. China supports the efforts of the Government and people of the Central African Republic to maintain stability, extend State authority and advance the peace process. We reaffirm our respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic and for the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs.

The sanctions regime should remain targeted, time-bound and subject to regular review. It should not impede the legitimate security and development efforts of the Central African Republic or affect the humanitarian situation. We welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) and support fair and clear procedures for listing and delisting. The Panel of Experts should carry out its mandate objectively and impartially, on the basis of verified information and in close cooperation with the Government of the Central African Republic, and its recommendations should respect the country’s ownership.

The international community should continue to support the Central African Republic in line with its national priorities and through African-led and regional mechanisms. China will continue to support the peace, stability and development of the Central African Republic.
after.France:
France welcomes the Council’s unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for the Central African Republic. I thank all members of the Council for their constructive engagement and for preserving the unity of the Council in support of the Central African Republic’s stabilization efforts.

France reaffirms its commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic. We recall the importance of full and effective implementation of the 2019 Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation, including through an inclusive political process with the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth.

The measures renewed today remain targeted. They are aimed at individuals and entities who threaten peace and stability in the Central African Republic, while preserving the humanitarian exemption established by resolution 2664 (2022). France stresses the importance of safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access and of ensuring that sanctions do not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance to those in need.

We also stress the importance of fair and clear procedures for listing and delisting, and we support the continued work of the Panel of Experts on the basis of verified and objective information. France will continue to work with all Council members and with the Government of the Central African Republic to support peace, accountability and stability in the country and the region.
after.Guyana: Guyana voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for the Central African Republic as important tools to support peace, stability and accountability. We welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) and stress that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate, time-bound and subject to regular review, with fair and clear delisting procedures. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, ensure full, safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and prevent grave violations against children. We encourage the Panel to continue basing its work on verified information and to cooperate closely with the Government of the Central African Republic and regional partners, including the African Union and ECCAS. Guyana reaffirms its commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic and to the full implementation of the 2019 Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation, including the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth.
after.Pakistan: Pakistan voted in favour of this resolution. We welcome its unanimous adoption and thank France for its efforts to facilitate consensus. Pakistan supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain useful tools in support of peace and stability in the Central African Republic. At the same time, sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate and time-bound, and should be implemented with full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of the Central African Republic and the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. We welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) and the emphasis on fair and clear delisting procedures. We encourage the Panel of Experts to base its work on verified and objective information and to cooperate closely with the Government of the Central African Republic and regional organizations, including the African Union and ECCAS. The international community should continue to support the Central African Republic’s national ownership, the full implementation of the 2019 Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation, the protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. Pakistan remains committed to supporting peace and security in Africa.
after.Republic of Korea: Thank you, Mr. President. The Republic of Korea voted in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for the Central African Republic, which remain important tools for supporting the country’s peace and stabilization efforts, preventing the diversion of arms and promoting accountability. At the same time, sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate and time-bound, with fair and clear procedures and full respect for the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022). We reaffirm our respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, unity and political independence of the Central African Republic and for the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. We call on all parties to fully implement the 2019 Political Agreement, protect civilians, ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access and cooperate with the Panel of Experts. The Republic of Korea will continue to support the Central African Republic’s efforts for peace, stability and development, in cooperation with regional and international partners.
after.Sierra Leone:
Thank you, Mr President. Sierra Leone voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We thank France for its penholder role and for the inclusive consultations that led to this outcome.

Sierra Leone welcomes the renewal of the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for the Central African Republic. As a country that has emerged from conflict and remains deeply engaged in peacebuilding, we know that sanctions must remain targeted, time-bound and subject to fair and clear procedures. We therefore welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) and stress that humanitarian assistance must reach all those in need in accordance with humanitarian principles.

We also reaffirm our strong commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of the Central African Republic. The measures adopted today should support, not impede, national efforts to extend State authority, protect civilians and implement the 2019 Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, cease violations and abuses, and ensure the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth in peace and political processes.

Sierra Leone encourages continued cooperation between the Panel of Experts, the Government of the Central African Republic, the African Union, ECCAS and all relevant stakeholders. We remain committed to peace, security and stability in the Central African Republic and across the African continent.
after.Slovenia: Slovenia voted in favour of this resolution. We welcome its unanimous adoption, which renews the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for the Central African Republic. We support this renewal because it contributes to accountability for armed groups, the protection of civilians, and respect for international humanitarian law, while preserving the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) so that life-saving assistance can reach those in need without undue impediment. Slovenia stresses that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate and subject to fair and clear procedures, and that the Panel’s reporting should continue to be based on verified and objective information. We reaffirm our strong support for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic, and we call for the full implementation of the 2019 Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation, including the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth. We encourage the Government of the Central African Republic and all partners to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel of Experts in support of peace, stability and accountability.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. We voted in favour because renewing the targeted sanctions and the mandate of the Panel of Experts supports the Central African Republic’s peace and stability, strengthens accountability for armed groups and those who violate international law, and helps protect humanitarian access. We welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), and we stress that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate and subject to fair and clear procedures. We call on all parties to implement the 2019 Political Agreement, protect civilians, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access and cooperate fully with the Panel. The United Kingdom remains committed to the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of the Central African Republic and to supporting an inclusive political process, including credible and peaceful elections.
after.United States of America: The United States welcomes the adoption of this resolution and thanks France for its work as penholder. We were pleased to vote in favour of renewing the targeted travel-ban and asset-freeze measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for the Central African Republic. These tools remain important for constraining armed groups, curbing illicit arms flows, and supporting accountability, while the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) ensures that lifesaving assistance can continue. We stress that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate, and subject to fair and clear procedures. The United States urges the Government of the Central African Republic to continue its cooperation with the Committee and the Panel, to fully implement the 2019 Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation, to pursue transparent and credible elections, and to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel and ensure safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access. We also encourage the Panel to continue reporting on the basis of verified information, including on illicit arms diversion, the exploitation of natural resources, and the activities of foreign fighters and mercenaries, as mandated. The United States remains committed to supporting the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and stability of the Central African Republic.
